question: Which type of nutrient is especially important for the baby's brain and nervous system growth?

options.A: Water
options.B: Fats
options.C: Starch
options.D: Fiber

explanation: Healthy dietary fats are superstars here! They provide essential fatty acids that build brain tissue and support your baby's developing nervous system.

question: A nurse notices pressure sores are common in the elderly ward and tries a new turning schedule. What is this an example of?

options.A: An illegal medical experiment on vulnerable human subjects
options.B: A quality improvement project based on clinical observation
options.C: A violation of hospital administrative policy
options.D: A financial investment in medical equipment manufacturing

explanation: Spot on! Noticing a ward problem and trying a practical nursing fix to make things better is a classic quality improvement project.

question: Bacterial vaginosis (BV) happens when there is an overgrowth of which specific organism?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Candida albicans
options.C: Trichomonas vaginalis
options.D: Gardnerella vaginalis

explanation: You got it! Gardnerella vaginalis and other anaerobic bacteria multiply too much in BV, pushing out our helpful flora. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h2)

question: What is the main job of a social worker on a community health team?

options.A: Reviewing lab results for abnormal electrolyte levels
options.B: Connecting families to housing and financial support
options.C: Performing surgical procedures in the clinic
options.D: Prescribing medications for high blood pressure

explanation: You got it! Social workers are pros at linking patients to resources outside the clinic that make daily life easier.

question: What makes a disease communicable?

options.A: It only affects people living in tropical climates.
options.B: It can be spread from one person or host to another.
options.C: It is caused strictly by genetic mutations in the body.
options.D: It cannot be prevented by standard hygiene practices.

explanation: You've got this! Communicable diseases simply mean infections that can jump or spread from an infected person to someone else. Keep up the great work!

question: Where does fertilization of the egg by a sperm cell usually take place?

options.A: Within the lower cervical canal
options.B: Inside the main cavity of the uterus
options.C: On the outer surface of the ovary
options.D: Ampulla of the fallopian tube

explanation: The wider ampulla section of the fallopian tube provides the right space and environment for the sperm to meet and fertilize the egg. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T1#GNS216_U2_T1_h5)

question: If your patient is very thin and malnourished, how might you adjust your subcutaneous technique?

options.A: The injection must be given at a 90-degree angle always
options.B: The medication must be diluted with sterile water first
options.C: A longer needle must be used to reach the fat layer
options.D: A shorter needle and a shallower insertion angle may be needed

explanation: Exactly! Thin patients have less fat padding, so using a shorter needle or a 45-degree angle helps make sure you don't accidentally go straight into the muscle.

question: Which of these is NOT a feature of anaphylactic shock?

options.A: Bronchospasm
options.B: Severe hypertension
options.C: Profound hypotension
options.D: Laryngeal edema

explanation: Correct! Anaphylaxis causes blood vessels to dilate widely and leak fluid, leading to severe *hypotension* (low blood pressure), not high blood pressure.

question: Why are elderly patients much more likely to get seriously dehydrated than younger adults?

options.A: They consume strictly dry foods with zero moisture content
options.B: Their kidneys completely stop producing urine as they age
options.C: They often have a reduced sense of thirst and less total body water reserve
options.D: Their skin absorbs environmental moisture instead of retaining internal fluids

explanation: Spot on! As people age, their natural feeling of thirst gets weaker, and they hold less water in their bodies, so they can dry out before they even realize they are thirsty.

question: When does an Rh-negative person usually develop anti-Rh antibodies?

options.A: After direct exposure to Rh-positive blood
options.B: Only after multiple pregnancies regardless of blood type
options.C: Naturally during the first few weeks of life
options.D: Before birth while inside the womb

explanation: Remember, unlike ABO antibodies which are present naturally, Rh antibodies only form after the immune system has its first contact with Rh-positive cells. Great job learning this! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h3)

question: In patients with high blood pressure, what common recovery factor can trigger a dangerous blood pressure spike?

options.A: Pain and anxiety
options.B: Sleeping on the left side
options.C: Eating fresh vegetables
options.D: Drinking too much water

explanation: When a patient feels pain or emotional stress, their nervous system kicks in, which can cause their blood pressure to shoot up.

question: What is the main way azole antifungal drugs work?

options.A: Creating physical holes in the outer cell membrane
options.B: Preventing the conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol
options.C: Destroying the chitin layer of suppuration
options.D: Preventing the uptake of vital glucose molecules

explanation: Well done! Azoles block a key enzyme needed to make ergosterol. Without enough ergosterol, the fungal cell membrane weakens and fails.

question: How can nurses best help alleviate the mental stress of patients in quarantine?

options.A: By telling them that their fears are completely irrational
options.B: By offering active listening, reassurance, and ways to stay connected with loved ones
options.C: By restricting all telephone and internet access for safety reasons
options.D: By avoiding any conversation about why they are confined

explanation: Maintaining social connection and offering empathetic communication significantly reduces psychological distress. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why do inherited degenerative brain diseases often change a person's emotions as well as their body?

options.A: The genetic mutations directly damage brain areas controlling mood and personality
options.B: Brain cell loss only happens in areas that control muscle movement
options.C: Medications used for movement problems always cause severe anger
options.D: Patients simply feel sad because they know they have a chronic illness

explanation: Think of it this way: when the disease targets specific brain pathways, it affects both how the body moves and how emotions are regulated. Makes total sense when you picture it! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h1)

question: What smart strategy helps protect a DRF against rising market prices?

options.A: Periodic and responsible review of drug selling prices
options.B: Giving free credit to all patients who request it
options.C: Stopping the purchase of expensive imported medications
options.D: Selling all essential drugs at a 90% discount

explanation: Adjusting prices sensibly helps the fund keep up with replacement costs so the pharmacy never runs dry.

question: What is a 'windshield survey' in community health nursing?

options.A: Measuring air pollution levels near busy highways
options.B: Interviewing motor vehicle drivers about road traffic accidents
options.C: Testing the windshields of ambulances for proper safety glass
options.D: Observing community conditions firsthand while moving through the area

explanation: A windshield survey is an observational method where the nurse drives or walks through a community to collect visual data about housing, environment, and resources. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h7)

question: A poorly nourished patient is admitted with a severe stomach infection. What physical change makes it easier for germs to get into their blood?

options.A: Increased production of white blood cells
options.B: Damage to the protective lining of the intestines
options.C: Rapid thickening of the stomach lining
options.D: Overproduction of protective stomach acid

explanation: Correct! Lacking enough protein weakens the gut wall, allowing bacteria and toxins to slip past the body's barriers into the bloodstream.

question: What is a major challenge for proper waste management in clinics with limited resources?

options.A: Strict enforcement of international laws
options.B: Excessive funding and overstaffing
options.C: Shortages of proper segregation supplies and erratic electricity
options.D: Too many advanced incinerators

explanation: Lack of steady power and basic items like safety boxes can make sticking to textbook waste rules tough in everyday rural practice.

question: In a healthcare setting, what does 'resource allocation' mean?

options.A: Calculating the exact profit made by a pharmacy
options.B: The process of admitting patients to private rooms
options.C: Writing new nursing textbooks for students
options.D: How funds, staff, and supplies are distributed

explanation: Great! Resource allocation is simply deciding how to share out available money, materials, and staff to where they are needed most.

question: What crucial instruction should a nurse give a patient taking prescribed corticosteroid therapy?

options.A: Stop the medication immediately if you start to feel better
options.B: Never stop taking the medication suddenly without medical guidance
options.C: Increase your daily salt intake to balance the steroid effects
options.D: Take the pills on an empty stomach right before bedtime

explanation: Abruptly stopping steroids can trigger a dangerous adrenal crisis because the body stops producing its own natural stress hormones during treatment. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h7)

question: How can a large youth population become a 'demographic dividend' instead of an economic strain?

options.A: By encouraging mass emigration of young people abroad
options.B: By ignoring youth unemployment until they reach retirement age
options.C: Through heavy investments in education, health, and job creation
options.D: By restricting all youths from participating in the labor market

explanation: When we invest in our youth through good schools, healthcare, and jobs, they turn into a superpower for the economy instead of facing unemployment struggles.

question: What kind of healthcare service should form the solid base of a healthy community's health system?

options.A: Traditional herbal medicine centers exclusively
options.B: Private specialist clinics for high-income earners
options.C: Primary healthcare focused on prevention and promotion
options.D: Expensive tertiary care hospitals with advanced surgery

explanation: Primary care brings basic check-ups, vaccines, and health education right to the grassroots where people live.

question: What do we call the normal vaginal discharge that a mother passes as her uterus heals after birth?

options.A: Lochia
options.B: Colostrum
options.C: Leukorrhea
options.D: Smegma

explanation: Lochia is just the body's natural way of cleaning out the uterus after delivery—shedding old tissue and blood as healing takes place.

question: Which body regulates nursing and midwifery practice in Nigeria?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.B: Pharmacists Council of National Health
options.C: Medical and Dental Consultants Association
options.D: National Union of Allied Health Workers

explanation: That's right! The NMCN sets the standards for our training and practice across the country.

question: Why are patients told to drink water and hold their urine before a pelvic ultrasound?

options.A: A full bladder pushes pelvic organs up into a better viewing position
options.B: To encourage bowel movements before the scan
options.C: A full bladder is needed to turn on the color Doppler
options.D: To stop them from getting dehydrated during the test

explanation: A distended bladder acts like a clear window, pushing gas-out of the way and giving a fantastic view of pelvic structures.

question: A nurse and a doctor argue because both want to decide the exact time to discharge a patient. What is the root cause here?

options.A: An absolute surplus of transport vehicles
options.B: Identical professional backgrounds
options.C: Role ambiguity and power imbalance
options.D: A complete lack of patient admission records

explanation: When two professionals clash over who has the final say, it usually means their job boundaries overlap and power is being contested.

question: Who is the focus of medical isolation compared to quarantine?

options.A: Travelers arriving from a foreign country
options.B: People who are currently sick with an infection
options.C: Healthcare workers who finished their shift
options.D: Healthy family members of a sick patient

explanation: Isolation separates individuals who already have a confirmed or suspected active infection from others. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h2)

question: Who should be involved when setting rehabilitation goals for a patient with a degenerative disorder?

options.A: Only the physical therapist and the patient
options.B: The healthcare team, the patient, and their family
options.C: Only the doctor and the hospital administrator
options.D: The insurance provider and the nursing supervisor

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Effective goal setting requires input from everyone involved in the patient's care to ensure targets are realistic and meaningful.

question: What actually happens in heart valve stenosis?

options.A: An infection develops on the inner lining of the heart
options.B: The valve opening narrows and makes it hard for blood to push through
options.C: The valve flaps fail to close tightly, letting blood leak backward
options.D: The heart valve fails to form at all before birth

explanation: Stenosis means narrowing. A stenotic valve is stiff and tight, making the heart push extra hard to get blood through the opening.

question: What are the small bumps on the areola called that secrete a protective fluid?

options.A: Montgomery glands
options.B: Lymph nodes
options.C: Sweat glands
options.D: Thyroid follicles

explanation: Montgomery glands are sebaceous glands located on the areola that keep the skin lubricated and healthy. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h2)

question: What is the most critical absolute contraindication for a standard barium swallow test?

options.A: Controlled type 2 diabetes
options.B: Suspected gastrointestinal perforation
options.C: A history of seasonal allergies
options.D: Mild chronic hypertension

explanation: If barium leaks outside a torn or perforated gut wall into the body cavities, it causes a severe, dangerous inflammatory reaction. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h2)

question: You check a new mother and notice her uterus feels soft and is pushed over to the right side. What should you do first?

options.A: Assist the patient to empty her bladder
options.B: Massage the calves to prevent clots
options.C: Administer a blood transfusion immediately
options.D: Encourage heavy ambulation around the ward

explanation: A full bladder acts like a bully, pushing the uterus upward and to the side and stopping it from contracting properly. Helping her pee often fixes the problem instantly! Great nursing intuition. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h3)

question: How does hyperparathyroidism usually impact a patient's bones?

options.A: It forces extra calcium to deposit, making bones overly thick
options.B: It triggers rapid bone growth that crushes nearby nerve roots
options.C: It stops blood flow to the joints, causing cartilage to melt
options.D: It pulls calcium out of bones, making them weak and painful

explanation: Too much parathyroid hormone acts like a withdrawal slip, pulling calcium right out of the skeleton and leaving bones fragile and aching.

question: A patient has acute Hepatitis B. Which part of their history helps you trace how they caught it?

options.A: Swimming in a public pool with high chlorine levels
options.B: Eating unwashed raw vegetables from a local market stall
options.C: Receiving an unscreened blood transfusion or sharing needles
options.D: Drinking untreated well water during a rural community visit

explanation: Spot on! Hepatitis B is a bloodborne infection, meaning it spreads through contact with infected blood or sharp objects like needles and unsterilized blades.

question: During a laryngoscopy, a patient's oxygen level suddenly drops from 98% to 85%. What is your immediate action as the nurse?

options.A: Administer an oral pain medication to relax the vocal cords.
options.B: Document the drop in the chart and wait for the doctor to finish looking.
options.C: Alert the clinician, stop the procedure, and provide supplemental oxygen or bag-valve-mask ventilation.
options.D: Ask the patient to sit up straight and take three deep breaths through their mouth.

explanation: Safety first! A sudden drop in oxygen means you must stop what's happening right away, get help, and give the patient oxygen.

question: Why are geriatric syndromes described as having multiple causes?

options.A: They result from impairments across multiple body systems
options.B: They are exclusively caused by psychological stress
options.C: They are caused by a single specific bacterial pathogen
options.D: They only occur in patients with genetic mutations

explanation: Geriatric syndromes (like falls or confusion) usually happen when little things go wrong across different parts of the body all at once, rather than just one single disease.

question: Why must nurses keep a close eye on blood sugar levels for patients on high-dose IV steroids, even if they don't have diabetes?

options.A: Steroids destroy pancreatic beta cells within the first few hours
options.B: Steroids cause severe dehydration that artificially concentrates sugar
options.C: Steroids increase the patient's appetite for high-sugar foods
options.D: Steroids stimulate glucose production and impair insulin utilization

explanation: Steroids encourage the liver to release more glucose while making body cells temporarily ignore insulin. This combo naturally causes blood sugar to rise!

question: Why is family counseling so valuable when coping with a progressive illness?

options.A: It forces family members to move into the same household
options.B: It eliminates all future disagreements about financial matters
options.C: It helps resolve conflicts and adjust roles regarding care responsibilities
options.D: It proves which family member caused the inherited genetic mutation

explanation: As illnesses progress, family roles shift. Counseling gives everyone a safe space to talk openly and share the care burden smoothly.

question: Why do past surgeries in the tummy make a new laparoscopy trickier?

options.A: Dense scar tissue increases the risk of organ injury during entry
options.B: The patient will require a much higher dose of antibiotics
options.C: Carbon dioxide gas cannot be absorbed through scarred tissue
options.D: Special cameras are unable to function in scarred abdomens

explanation: You're learning fast! Old surgeries leave behind scar tissue (adhesions) that can pull intestines closer to the tummy wall, making it easier to accidentally nick them during instrument entry.

question: A woman in labor in a remote village has a uterine rupture, but the family cannot find a vehicle to take her to the hospital. Which delay does this represent?

options.A: Delay in diagnosing the initial pregnancy
options.B: Delay in receiving adequate treatment at the hospital
options.C: Delay in deciding to seek care
options.D: Delay in reaching a medical facility

explanation: You nailed it. Distance, bad roads, and transport troubles fall squarely under the second delay—getting from home to a health facility.

question: What are the three parts of the epidemiological triad used to study how diseases spread?

options.A: Infection, disease, and recovery
options.B: Pathogen, vector, and symptom
options.C: Agent, host, and environment
options.D: Human, animal, and bacteria

explanation: Think of the triad as a stool with three legs: the infectious agent, the susceptible host, and the environment. All three must interact for an infection to take root!

question: Which of these behaviors counts as psychological or emotional violence under the VAPP Act?

options.A: Constant intimidation and stalking
options.B: Forgetting to buy household groceries
options.C: Accidental physical injury from sports
options.D: Failing a school promotion examination

explanation: Correct! Mental torture, constant threats, intimidation, and stalking are all forms of psychological abuse covered by the law.

question: Which of these is a major socioeconomic challenge that can make storing home medications very difficult?

options.A: Too many professional nursing visits in one week
options.B: Unstable housing or lack of reliable electricity
options.C: An overabundance of municipal transportation options
options.D: Excessive amounts of local community food banks

explanation: Exactly. Think of medications like insulin—without stable electricity or a fridge, keeping them safe at home becomes a huge hurdle.

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks suddenly experiences painless vaginal bleeding. What condition should immediately come to mind?

options.A: Preeclampsia
options.B: Placenta previa
options.C: Placental abruption
options.D: Uterine rupture

explanation: A classic clinical clue! Bright red, painless bleeding in the late second or third trimester is the textbook sign of placenta previa.

question: A nurse sets up a quick blood sugar check station at the local market. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Primordial prevention
options.B: Tertiary prevention
options.C: Primary prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: Awesome! Screening tests help us spot hidden or early-stage health issues, making this secondary prevention.

question: What is most likely to happen if a new DRF launches with too little seed capital?

options.A: Patients will receive completely free medications for life
options.B: The government will stop taxing local pharmaceutical companies
options.C: The pharmacy will experience immediate stock-outs due to low inventory
options.D: The facility will automatically make massive profits in the first week

explanation: Spot on! If you start with too little inventory, you can't meet patient needs, and the system stalls before it even really begins.

question: A postoperative patient who had surgery for a ruptured ectopic pregnancy suddenly becomes pale, dizzy, and has a dropping blood pressure. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.A: Call for emergency medical help and ensure large IV lines are open for fluids
options.B: Help the patient get out of bed and walk around the room to improve circulation
options.C: Offer the patient a warm cup of tea and a light snack to boost her energy
options.D: Wait quietly for the next scheduled doctor's round in the morning

explanation: Signs of declining blood pressure and dizziness point to hemorrhage and shock, requiring immediate emergency response and fluid resuscitation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of the National Drug Policy in Nigeria?

options.A: To ensure medicines are safe, effective, and properly used
options.B: To give nurses the sole legal power to write prescriptions
options.C: To make every single medication free for all citizens
options.D: To stop all foreign pharmaceutical companies from importing drugs

explanation: The policy sets standards to protect the public by regulating drug quality, distribution, and rational use. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the leading cause of unintentional injury death among adolescents worldwide?

options.A: Accidental poisonings
options.B: Road traffic crashes
options.C: Unsupervised drownings
options.D: Severe electrical shocks

explanation: Well done! Road traffic crashes consistently rank as the top cause of accidental injury deaths among teenagers globally.

question: What does 'values clarification' help a nurse examine?

options.A: Hospital equipment inventory
options.B: Monthly salary deductions
options.C: Personal beliefs and biases
options.D: Public transport schedules

explanation: Values clarification is a great self-check tool. It allows us as nurses to look at our own inner biases so our personal opinions never get in the way of great patient care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h2)

question: What is the main goal of giving ovulation-stimulating medications like clomiphene citrate?

options.A: To thicken the uterine lining permanently
options.B: To clear blocked fallopian tubes
options.C: To increase male testosterone levels
options.D: To encourage the release of mature eggs

explanation: These helpful drugs nudge the ovaries to develop and release eggs when a woman's ovulation is irregular.

question: What does arterial bleeding typically look like?

options.A: Clear fluid mixed with streaks of old blood
options.B: Slowly oozing blood that stops without pressure
options.C: Bright red blood that spurts with each heartbeat
options.D: Dark red blood that flows in a steady stream

explanation: Arteries carry oxygenated blood under high pressure straight from the heart, causing it to spurt when they are cut. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why is assessing the oral cavity a routine part of a general physical examination?

options.A: It is the only reliable way to measure a patient's exact daily caloric intake.
options.B: It allows the nurse to directly test the function of the respiratory lungs.
options.C: It gives quick clues about a patient's hydration, nutrition, and systemic health.
options.D: It confirms whether the patient has completely normal kidney filtration rates.

explanation: Oral tissues react quickly to changes in fluid balance, nutrition, and general disease, making the mouth a window into overall health. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h1)

question: A 15-year-old girl comes to the clinic with her older husband, showing bruises and sadness. How should the nurse care for her?

options.A: Scold the husband in front of the patient and demand they divorce immediately
options.B: Report the family to the hospital billing department for financial investigation
options.C: Use a trauma-informed approach, ensure privacy for screening, and connect her with social support
options.D: Treat the physical bruises quickly and send them home without asking further questions

explanation: You've got it! Keeping her safe, checking her emotional needs, and involving social services is the hallmark of great, compassionate nursing.

question: A home health nurse enters a poorly lit room with loose floor mats to check a frail patient. What is the immediate priority?

options.A: Wait in the vehicle until the family completely remodels the flooring
options.B: Address or remove the tripping hazards before performing the clinical assessment
options.C: Ignore the environment and focus only on checking the patient's pulse
options.D: Call emergency services to report a hazardous building violation

explanation: Ensuring physical safety by removing hazards prevents falls for both the vulnerable patient and the visiting nurse. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of an adult day care home?

options.A: To offer permanent residential housing for older adults
options.B: To serve as a 24-hour acute care hospital ward
options.C: To provide specialized surgical interventions
options.D: To provide daytime supervised care and support services

explanation: Adult day care homes are specifically designed to offer structured programs, supervision, and support during daytime hours while allowing clients to return home at night. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h1)

question: A patient died with an IV line in place and a coroner's post-mortem is requested. What should the nurse do with the line?

options.A: Hide the lines under the bedsheets
options.B: Remove all lines immediately to clean the skin
options.C: Leave all lines and tubes in place
options.D: Cut the tubing short and tape it down

explanation: For coroner's cases or potential legal investigations, invasive lines and tubes must be left intact for the pathologist. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h4)

question: What is another common name for Type III FGM?

options.A: Excision
options.B: Defibulation
options.C: Clitoridectomy
options.D: Infibulation

explanation: Type III is widely called infibulation because the procedure creates a sealed covering over the vaginal opening.

question: Why is natural daylight or color-corrected light best when checking a patient's skin?

options.A: It eliminates the need to wear protective examination gloves
options.B: It magnifies tiny skin lesions without needing specialized glass tools
options.C: It prevents misinterpreting subtle color changes like jaundice or cyanosis
options.D: It ensures the patient stays warm during a full physical examination

explanation: Yellow room lights can trick your eyes, making it hard to spot important color changes like yellow skin (jaundice) or a bluish tint (cyanosis).

question: What does 'shared decision-making' mean in nursing?

options.A: The patient deciding on treatments without any input from healthcare staff
options.B: The nurse making all clinical choices based solely on hospital policy
options.C: Family members making all health choices on behalf of the patient
options.D: Collaboration between the nurse and patient using clinical expertise and personal values

explanation: You got it! It's a true partnership where professional medical knowledge meets the patient's personal life values.

question: Where does developing true cultural competence in nursing actually begin?

options.A: Reading advanced textbooks on international medical laws
options.B: Memorizing every religious holiday observed in the country
options.C: Traveling to foreign countries to study local hospital systems
options.D: Recognizing one's own personal biases and cultural assumptions

explanation: Spot on! Self-awareness is key. You first have to understand your own background and biases so they don't mess with the care you give others.

question: Why does a recipient's immune system try to attack a newly transplanted organ?

options.A: It panics over the physical pressure of the new blood flow
options.B: It causes a sudden crash in red blood cells
options.C: It spots foreign human leukocyte antigens (HLAs) on the donor cells
options.D: It reacts badly to the surgical stitches

explanation: Our immune systems are super protective! When they see foreign HLA markers on a donor organ that don't match the body's own, they sound the alarm and try to reject it.

question: Which skin layer contains the blood vessels, nerve endings, and collagen fibers?

options.A: Dermis
options.B: Hypodermis
options.C: Stratum corneum
options.D: Epidermis

explanation: The dermis is the vascularized middle layer of the skin that holds blood vessels, nerves, and tough connective tissue fibers. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the main difference between primary and acquired immune deficiencies?

options.A: Primary deficiencies are always mild, while acquired deficiencies are fatal.
options.B: Primary deficiencies are present at birth, while acquired deficiencies develop later in life.
options.C: Acquired deficiencies can be cured with vitamins, but primary deficiencies cannot.
options.D: Primary deficiencies affect only red blood cells, while acquired deficiencies affect white cells.

explanation: Spot on! Primary immune conditions are inherited and present right from birth, whereas acquired ones happen due to outside factors later in life.

question: Which machine uses high-pressure steam to sterilize infectious items?

options.A: Autoclaving
options.B: Incineration
options.C: Municipal landfilling
options.D: Chemical burial

explanation: An autoclave uses hot, pressurized steam to completely destroy all microorganisms on contaminated equipment before it gets reused or discarded.

question: A nurse is preparing to insert an indwelling urinary catheter. Which type of technique must be used?

options.A: Surgical asepsis
options.B: Universal decontamination
options.C: Standard sanitation
options.D: Medical asepsis

explanation: Catheterization enters the sterile urinary tract, requiring surgical asepsis to prevent introducing bacteria into the bladder. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the absolute gold standard method to confirm an NG tube is sitting correctly?

options.A: Abdominal X-ray confirmation
options.B: Auscultating an air bolus over the stomach
options.C: Observing condensation inside the clear plastic tube
options.D: Checking if the patient can speak clearly

explanation: An X-ray never guesses! It gives you a clear picture of exactly where the tube tip is resting, making it the top gold standard.

question: What is the purpose of comparing local community health statistics with national standards?

options.A: To prove that national health policies are completely useless
options.B: To eliminate the need for conducting household surveys
options.C: To punish the local health workers for poor performance
options.D: To see where the local health indicators fall behind or exceed standard levels

explanation: Comparing local numbers to national data helps highlight specific areas where the community is suffering more than average. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why is an Rh-negative mother at risk when carrying an Rh-positive baby for the second time?

options.A: Her plasma lacks enough iron to support two separate blood supplies
options.B: Her immune system has already formed antibodies against the Rh factor
options.C: Her baby will automatically inherit a mismatched ABO blood type
options.D: Her bone marrow stops producing red blood cells during late pregnancy

explanation: Exposure during the first pregnancy sensitizes the mother, prompting her body to build antibodies that can attack a later Rh-positive baby. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h3)

question: What do we mean by 'closed-loop communication' during a busy medical emergency?

options.A: Repeating a delegated instruction back to the sender to confirm it was heard and understood
options.B: Writing all verbal orders on a whiteboard before speaking to team members
options.C: Turning off all ward intercoms so outside noise does not distract the team
options.D: Locking the patient room door so unauthorized staff cannot enter

explanation: Exactly! Saying 'Got it, giving 10mg IV now' back to the doctor or senior nurse prevents dangerous mistakes in high-stress moments.

question: What happens when someone gets a transfusion of the wrong, incompatible blood type?

options.A: The recipient's bone marrow stops producing new hemoglobin
options.B: Plasma proteins dissolve all white blood cells in the sample
options.C: Donor red blood cells undergo agglutination and hemolysis
options.D: Platelets instantly multiply to repair the blood vessels

explanation: You nailed it! The recipient's antibodies attack the foreign blood cells, causing them to clump together (agglutinate) and break apart (hemolysis).

question: How do research objectives connect to your main research question?

options.A: Objectives replace the research question entirely during data analysis
options.B: Objectives are guesses made before looking at the research question
options.C: Objectives explain why the research question is impossible to answer
options.D: Objectives break the main question down into smaller, actionable steps

explanation: Think of objectives as the stepping stones. They take your big main research question and slice it into smaller, bite-sized goals you can achieve one by one.

question: Which dangerous practice is often triggered by a shortage of disposable syringes?

options.A: Reusing disposable syringes or improper sterilization
options.B: Refusing to treat patients who arrive without insurance
options.C: Giving all medications exclusively through oral tablets
options.D: Storing vaccines at room temperature for weeks

explanation: Severe supply shortages often force facilities to reuse single-use equipment, drastically increasing infection rates. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h5)

question: What exactly is a nerve pathway?

options.A: An open space where hormones travel through the bloodstream
options.B: A blood vessel supplying oxygen directly to the brain cells
options.C: The protective fatty covering surrounding peripheral nerve fibers
options.D: The specific route electrical and chemical impulses travel through the nervous system

explanation: Think of a nerve pathway like a designated highway for your body's electrical signals, guiding messages smoothly from where they start to where they need to go!

question: Which of these is a critical warning sign that a pregnant woman must report straight away?

options.A: Occasional mild heartburn
options.B: Decreased fetal movement
options.C: Increased fatigue in the evening
options.D: Mild swelling in the ankles

explanation: Always teach mums to track their baby's kicks! Fewer movements can mean the baby is stressed and needs an immediate check-up.

question: What is the go-to emergency medication for a patient in acute anaphylactic shock?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Salbutamol inhaler
options.C: Diphenhydramine
options.D: Hydrocortisone

explanation: Epinephrine is a lifesaver in anaphylaxis! It quickly tightens blood vessels, opens up tight airways, and keeps the heart pumping.

question: What is the primary purpose of a gastrostomy feeding tube?

options.A: To deliver nutrition directly into the stomach
options.B: To provide continuous intravenous hydration
options.C: To bypass the small intestine during digestion
options.D: To remove excess air and fluid from the bowel

explanation: A gastrostomy tube places food and fluids straight into the stomach, bypassing the mouth and esophagus for patients who cannot swallow safely. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which level of prevention stops risk factors from even starting through broad social and economic policies?

options.A: Clinical rehabilitation
options.B: Secondary prevention
options.C: Primordial prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: Primordial prevention is all about stopping risk factors before they even take root in a society through broad policies.

question: A nursing mother says her milk suddenly stops flowing when she gets stressed or anxious in a crowded room. Why does this happen?

options.A: Stress inhibits the release of oxytocin, preventing the let-down reflex.
options.B: High adrenaline levels directly destroy colostrum inside the lactiferous ducts.
options.C: Anxiety causes prolactin receptors in the alveoli to temporarily close.
options.D: Fear triggers an immediate decrease in the systemic production of estrogen.

explanation: Stress and anxiety release adrenaline, which can block oxytocin. Without oxytocin, the milk doesn't 'let down,' even though it's inside the breast!

question: Roughly how many extra calories per day does producing breast milk require on average?

options.A: 100 calories
options.B: 1200 calories
options.C: 50 calories
options.D: 500 calories

explanation: Milk production is metabolically demanding, requiring about 500 extra calories daily for an exclusively breastfeeding mother. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T013#GNS227_U2_T013_h2)

question: Why do certain smells instantly trigger strong memories or emotions?

options.A: Smell signals pass through the visual cortex first
options.B: The nose shares a direct blood supply with the hippocampus
options.C: Odorants directly stimulate the motor strip in the frontal lobe
options.D: Olfactory pathways connect directly to the limbic system in the brain

explanation: You got it! Unlike other senses, smell signals bypass the brain's relay station (the thalamus) and go straight to emotional centers like the amygdala and hippocampus. That's why a scent can instantly remind you of home!

question: What does MUAC stand for in paediatric nutritional assessment?

options.A: Mid-Upper Arm Circumference
options.B: Minimum Urinary Acid Concentration
options.C: Mean Underweight Assessment Criteria
options.D: Maximum Upper Abdominal Capacity

explanation: MUAC is a super handy, quick measurement used by community nurses to screen children for acute malnutrition right on the spot!

question: If a mother has an umbilical cord prolapse, what position should you put her in right away?

options.A: Flat supine position with legs fully extended
options.B: Knee-chest or exaggerated Sims position
options.C: Left lateral position with head elevated high
options.D: Upright sitting position in a delivery chair

explanation: Gravity is key here! This position gets the baby's weight off the cord so oxygen can keep flowing while you prep for emergency help.

question: Why is community participation important in primary health care delivery?

options.A: It allows community members to write hospital prescriptions independently
options.B: It empowers people to take charge of their own health and ensures programs succeed
options.C: It prevents the government from ever building new health clinics
options.D: It reduces the salary budget required for employing trained nurses

explanation: When communities participate in their own healthcare solutions, health programs gain local ownership and long-term sustainability. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h6)

question: How did 20th-century pharmacology fundamentally differ from ancient healing practices?

options.A: It shifted from using crude natural mixtures to laboratory synthesis and targeted chemicals.
options.B: It abandoned all plant-based treatments in favor of spiritual healing.
options.C: It stopped testing medications on living tissues before human use.
options.D: It relied exclusively on oral traditions rather than written science.

explanation: Twentieth-century science moved past trial-and-error plant use to design and synthesize targeted chemical compounds in laboratories. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why is good etiquette especially important when nursing inside a patient's home?

options.A: It replaces the need for actual clinical skills and assessments
options.B: It ensures the family will buy extra medical supplies for the patient
options.C: It helps the nurse balance being a polite guest with upholding professional standards
options.D: It prevents the patient from asking questions about their medications

explanation: Brilliant! You are a guest in their home, but you are also a trained clinician. Good etiquette helps you respect their space while still doing your job safely.

question: What should be clearly recorded in the patient's register when a standing order is used?

options.A: The specific protocol used, assessment findings, and treatments given
options.B: The political affiliation of the patient receiving care
options.C: The personal home address of the facility's medical director
options.D: A detailed financial profit statement for the pharmacy unit

explanation: Proper documentation requires noting the exact protocol followed, clinical findings, and interventions administered for legal and continuity purposes. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h7)

question: Which dimension of health involves the ability to handle daily stress and express feelings properly?

options.A: Spiritual dimension
options.B: Emotional dimension
options.C: Intellectual dimension
options.D: Environmental dimension

explanation: The emotional dimension focuses on mental resilience, coping mechanisms, and emotional expression. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is a common emotional reaction when a client suddenly cannot perform daily tasks on their own anymore?

options.A: Profound grief and loss of autonomy
options.B: Immediate acceptance of the new condition
options.C: Complete indifference to medical equipment
options.D: A sudden surge in physical stamina

explanation: It's tough losing your independence. Having to rely on others for basic chores often brings up deep grief and a feeling of losing control over one's own life.

question: What are the three classic steps in Kurt Lewin's model of change?

options.A: Unfreezing, moving, and refreezing
options.B: Denial, anger, and acceptance
options.C: Planning, executing, and evaluating
options.D: Assessing, diagnosing, and treating

explanation: Classic nursing management! Think of it like melting an ice block, shaping it into something new, and freezing it solid again.

question: Why is giving quick feedback so important when teaching clinical skills?

options.A: It ensures the school receives government funding
options.B: It prevents students from asking clinical questions
options.C: It replaces the need for formal written examinations
options.D: It connects the performance directly to the learning moment

explanation: If someone tells you what you did right or wrong right away, your brain connects with it immediately before you forget the details.

question: If a community health nurse notices that immunization rates remain low despite running a vaccination campaign, what should be done next?

options.A: Investigate the barriers causing the low uptake and adjust the strategy
options.B: Report the village to the police for failing to cooperate
options.C: Pretend the campaign was a success and submit fabricated data reports
options.D: Assume the community does not care about health and stop all programs

explanation: Evaluation is an ongoing feedback loop; when targets are missed, nurses must analyze the root causes and modify their approach. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h7)
